transcript.text: We had a power cut last night and now our Candy washer dryer is completely dead - no lights, nothing. Everything else in the house came back on. The plug fuse is fine, I swapped it. Help!

Since the plug fuse is fine and there are no lights at all, the issue is likely internal—often the main PCB (control board) or the power supply section within it. To identify the correct part or next steps, I need the model number. It is usually on a sticker inside the door rim or on the back of the door.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
It's a Candy Smart Pro, model CSOW 4965TWE/1-80 on the label. About 3 years old. I've also tried the socket with a lamp and it works fine, and unplugging it for 10+ minutes didn't help.

The most likely cause is a failure of the main control PCB (the brain of the machine), possibly triggered by the voltage spike from last night's power cut. As this involves opening the appliance casing to access internal electronics, it is not safe for you to repair yourself. I recommend contacting a qualified engineer or Candy support for a repair.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.

candidates: Internal power supply failure (PCB or transformer) (high)
Faulty mains lead or internal wiring break (medium)
